content: Adverse effects associated with the use of Vytorin, which contains ezetimibe and simvastatin, are detailed below. These effects are categorized based on clinical studies, post-marketing reports, and laboratory findings. Ezetimibe In placebo-controlled studies, the following adverse effects were reported with ezetimibe, regardless of whether they were directly caused by the drug: General disorders: Fatigue. Gastrointestinal disorders: Abdominal pain and diarrhea. Infections: Viral infections, pharyngitis, and sinusitis. Musculoskeletal disorders: Joint pain (arthralgia) and back pain. Respiratory disorders: Coughing. Post-Marketing Experience Adverse reactions reported after the drug was marketed include: Hypersensitivity reactions: These include anaphylaxis, angioedema, rash, and urticaria. Musculoskeletal issues: Joint pain (arthralgia) and muscle pain (myalgia). Liver-related issues: Elevated liver transaminases and hepatitis. Hematologic issues: Thrombocytopenia. Pancreatic issues: Pancreatitis. Gastrointestinal symptoms: Nausea. Neurological symptoms: Dizziness, paresthesia (tingling or numbness), and depression. Gallbladder-related issues: Gallstones (cholelithiasis) and gallbladder inflammation (cholecystitis). Muscle-related issues: Elevated creatine phosphokinase levels and, in rare cases, myopathy or rhabdomyolysis. Simvastatin Adverse effects reported in placebo-controlled clinical studies with simvastatin include: General disorders: Weakness (asthenia). Eye disorders: Cataracts. Gastrointestinal disorders: Abdominal pain, constipation, diarrhea, indigestion (dyspepsia), flatulence, and nausea. Skin disorders: Eczema, itching (pruritus), and rash. Additional effects reported with other HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors (statins), which may or may not be associated with simvastatin, include: Musculoskeletal disorders: Muscle cramps, muscle pain (myalgia), muscle disease (myopathy), severe muscle breakdown (rhabdomyolysis), and joint pain (arthralgia). Nervous system disorders: Cranial nerve dysfunction (e.g., altered taste, impaired eye movement, facial weakness), tremors, dizziness, memory loss, tingling or numbness (paresthesia), peripheral neuropathy, peripheral nerve palsy, and psychiatric disturbances. Ear disorders: Vertigo. Psychiatric disorders: Anxiety, insomnia, depression, and decreased libido. Hypersensitivity reactions: Rare hypersensitivity syndromes, including anaphylaxis, angioedema, lupus-like syndrome, polymyalgia rheumatica, dermatomyositis, vasculitis, purpura, thrombocytopenia, leukopenia, hemolytic anemia, positive antinuclear antibodies (ANA), increased erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR), eosinophilia, arthritis, joint pain (arthralgia), hives (urticaria), weakness (asthenia), photosensitivity, fever, chills, flushing, malaise, shortness of breath (dyspnea), toxic epidermal necrolysis, erythema multiforme, and Stevens-Johnson syndrome. Gastrointestinal disorders: Pancreatitis and vomiting. Liver-related issues: Hepatitis (including chronic active hepatitis), cholestatic jaundice, fatty liver changes, and, rarely, cirrhosis, fulminant hepatic necrosis, liver failure, or liver cancer (hepatoma). Metabolic disorders: Loss of appetite (anorexia). Skin disorders: Hair loss (alopecia), itching (pruritus), and various skin changes (e.g., nodules, discoloration, dryness, and changes to hair or nails). Reproductive disorders: Gynecomastia (enlarged male breast tissue) and erectile dysfunction. Eye disorders: Progression of cataracts and paralysis of eye muscles (ophthalmoplegia). Laboratory abnormalities: Elevated liver enzymes (transaminases), alkaline phosphatase, gamma-glutamyl transpeptidase (GGT), and bilirubin, as well as thyroid function abnormalities. Laboratory Tests Persistent and significant increases in serum transaminases have been observed in some patients. Approximately 5% of patients taking simvastatin experienced creatine kinase (CK) levels that were three or more times the normal value, though this was attributed to the non-cardiac fraction of CK. Muscle pain or dysfunction was generally not reported in these cases. Concomitant Lipid-Lowering Therapy In clinical studies where simvastatin was used alongside cholestyramine, no unique adverse reactions were observed beyond those already associated with either simvastatin or cholestyramine. Adolescent Patients In a 48-week study involving adolescents aged 10-17 years with heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia, the safety profile of simvastatin (10-40 mg daily) was similar to that of placebo. The most common adverse effects in both groups were upper respiratory infections, headaches, abdominal pain, and nausea.
